title: A.R. Rahman Just Performed at the India-Pakistan Border. No Artist Had Ever Done It Before.
excerpt: The Oscar winner turned the Attari Beating Retreat into a concert — opening with a new melody and closing with Maa Tujhe Salaam — as thousands of BSF jawans and visitors roared along.
body:
The sun was still high over the Attari Border Post on Saturday evening when A.R. Rahman walked onto the stage at JCP Stadium, looked out at thousands of BSF jawans and visitors packed into the stands, and did something no musician in Indian history had done before: he performed a live concert at the India-Pakistan border.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=pKaGtiGKDVs

The event, titled Jai Ho — A Musical Salute to the Bravehearts, was staged during the iconic Beating Retreat Ceremony — the same daily ritual where Indian and Pakistani soldiers lower their flags in choreographed unison. Except this time, there was a soundtrack. And it was composed by the man who wrote Jai Ho.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZSudrJjeJL/

A Set List Built for the Moment

Rahman opened with Chanda Suraj Lakhon Taare, a soulful, unreleased melody that silenced the stadium before the cheers erupted. The crowd — thousands of visitors who had come for the daily flag ceremony and found themselves at a once-in-a-lifetime concert instead — went quiet as his voice filled the Punjab evening. Then he pulled them into the world of Main Vaapas Aaunga, the upcoming Imtiaz Ali film that gave the concert its reason for being.

Vedang Raina — the young actor who plays the film's lead — joined him onstage for Maskara, bringing a raw, youthful energy that contrasted beautifully with Rahman's composed brilliance. Mohit Chauhan — the voice behind Tum Se Hi and Masakali, the man whose voice has soundtracked more heartbreaks than any singer alive — delivered a goosebump-inducing Ishq Mastana alongside vocalists Pooja Tiwari and Nargis. And then, to close, Rahman did the only thing he could do at a border ceremony honouring Indian soldiers: he played Maa Tujhe Salaam.

"This performance is an ode to the national spirit, to our bravehearts on the border, the BSF and the Indian Army, and to the spirit of solidarity and love that binds us all." — Imtiaz Ali

The stadium, by all accounts, lost it. BSF jawans in uniform. Families from Amritsar. Tourists who'd come for the daily spectacle and walked away having witnessed something historic. The atmosphere was electric — cheers, tears, and a profound sense of national pride that nobody in that stadium will forget.

Why the Border Matters for This Film

The location wasn't random. Main Vaapas Aaunga, releasing in theatres on June 12, is a Partition love story — the kind Imtiaz Ali has been circling his entire career. It follows a young poet named Keenu (Vedang Raina) and Jiya (Sharvari), whose romance blooms in an undivided India and is torn apart by 1947. Decades later, an aged Keenu (Naseeruddin Shah) wants to cross the border one last time to visit the hometown that's now in Pakistan. His grandson, played by Diljit Dosanjh, takes him.

The Attari Border — the same gate through which hundreds of thousands crossed during Partition, never to return — is literally the threshold of that story. Performing the film's music there, during the ceremony that symbolises the daily tension and ritual between the two nations, was a stroke of emotional genius. The makers also dedicated the film's entire music album — composed by Rahman with lyrics by the great Irshad Kamil — to India's armed forces.

"We bring a message of love because, ultimately, only love sustains us." — Imtiaz Ali

Ananya Birla of Birla Studios and producer Mohit Choudhary of Window Seat Films were also present, along with representatives from Applause Entertainment. The event was designed not as a press junket or a launch party, but as a genuine tribute — and by all reports, it felt like one.

What the Diaspora Should Know

For the millions of Indians abroad whose families carry Partition stories in their blood, this film is arriving at exactly the right frequency. It's Imtiaz Ali doing what he does best — wrapping enormous historical pain in intimate, personal love — but at a scale he hasn't attempted before. The cast alone — Naseeruddin Shah, Diljit Dosanjh, Sharvari, Vedang Raina — signals something serious.

Main Vaapas Aaunga releases worldwide on June 12, 2026. It's produced by Birla Studios, Applause Entertainment, and Window Seat Films. Music is on Tips Music. If the Attari concert is any indication, bring tissues.
author: Diaspora Desk
